headings.text: The map model in one minute
Receiving CoT and custom detail tags

blocks.html:
Two capabilities cover most of what plugins actually do: putting things on the map, and exchanging Cursor-on-Target (CoT) messages with the rest of the TAK network.

The map model in one minute

  • **MapView** — the map surface. Reach it from a receiver with getMapView().
  • **MapGroup** — a container/tree of map items. getMapView().getRootGroup() is the top of the tree; you can nest your own groups under it.
  • **MapItem** — anything on the map. Marker (a point with an icon/callsign) is the most common; there are also shapes, routes, rectangles, associations, etc.
  • **GeoPoint** — a lat/lon(/altitude) coordinate.

Adding an item to a group makes it appear (as we did in Build a UI); removing it hides it. That's the whole loop.

What CoT is

Cursor-on-Target (CoT) is the lingua franca of the TAK ecosystem — a compact event format describing what is where, when, by whom. Markers, drawings, routes, chat, and sensor data all travel between TAK clients and servers as CoT events. As a plugin author you rarely hand-write CoT XML; you convert ATAK map items to CotEvents and hand them to a dispatcher.

Internal vs external dispatch

ATAK exposes two dispatchers through CotMapComponent, and the distinction matters:

  • External dispatcher — sends the event out over the network to configured outputs (other clients, a TAK Server). Use this to share something with the team.
  • Internal dispatcher — routes the event through ATAK's own internal bus, as if the local app had just received it over the network. Use this to make the local ATAK process an event without transmitting it.

The example dispatches a drawing to the network like this:

// Convert an ATAK map item into a CoT event, then broadcast it externally.
final CotEvent cotEvent = CotEventFactory.createCotEvent(drawingRectangle);
CotMapComponent.getExternalDispatcher().dispatchToBroadcast(cotEvent);

• **CotEventFactory.createCotEvent(mapItem)** turns a MapItem into a CotEvent — you don't build the XML by hand.
  • **dispatchToBroadcast(cotEvent)** sends to all configured network outputs. There are also more targeted dispatch methods when you want to send to specific contacts rather than broadcasting.

To send to a specific TAK contact, the example builds on TAKContactSender / CotServiceRemote and ATAK's contact list rather than broadcasting to everyone — see HelloWorldContactSender in the example.

Receiving CoT and custom detail tags

Incoming CoT is delivered to ATAK and turned into map items automatically. When you need to attach custom data to events — your own XML "detail" sub-elements that ATAK doesn't understand natively — register a CotDetailHandler with the CotDetailManager:

CotDetailManager.getInstance().registerHandler(
    new CotDetailHandler("__myDetail") {
        // INBOUND: a received CoT carried your detail → copy it onto the map item
        @Override
        public CommsMapComponent.ImportResult toItemMetadata(
                MapItem item, CotEvent event, CotDetail detail) {
            // read detail, set metadata on item
            return CommsMapComponent.ImportResult.SUCCESS;
        }

        // OUTBOUND: an item is being turned into CoT → add your detail element
        @Override
        public boolean toCotDetail(MapItem item, CotEvent event, CotDetail root) {
            // append your <__myDetail .../> element to root
            return true;
        }
    });

This handler pair — toItemMetadata (inbound) and toCotDetail (outbound) — is how a plugin teaches ATAK to round-trip its own data through the CoT network without breaking interoperability with other clients.

Register detail handlers in your MapComponent.onCreate and unregister them in your cleanup, so they live exactly as long as your plugin does.
